newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO calls on Milosevic to re-instate elections.
newsitem.headline: NATO calls on Milosevic to re-instate elections.

text.p: NATO on Tuesday "strongly deplored" the Serbian government's cancellation of local election results last month and called on President Slobodan Milosevic to reverse the decision.

"We are dismayed that the Serbian authorities have ignored the calls of the international community to respect internationally recognised democratic principles," the 16 NATO members said in a statement.

The statement, issued shortly after the start of a two-day meeting of NATO foreign ministers, also praised the restraint of the Serbian opposition, which has mounted peaceful mass protests against Milosevic's decision.
"We commend the opposition for its adherence to non-violence and call upon the government to avoid any use of force against the peaceful protestors," it said.

Earlier, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher warned Milosevic -- once seen as vital to implementation of the Dayton peace accord in Bosnia -- he faced international isolation unless he respected democratic norms.
"The people of Serbia deserve what their neighbours in central Europe have: clean elections, a free press, a normal market economy," Christopher told the meeting.

"If President Milosevic respects their will, Serbia can enjoy the legitimacy and assistance it needs. If he seeks to rule Serbia as un unreformed dictatorship, it will only increase his isolation and the suffering of his people."

An opposition coalition claimed widespread victories in the November 17 elections, winning control of Belgrade and 14 other major cities. But a Serbian court cancelled the results and Milosevic has so far shown no sign of reinstating them.

Serbian opposition parties lost a legal battle for control of Belgrade's urban government on Tuesday when the Yugoslav federal supreme court refused to hear their claims of election fraud by the ruling socialists.
At a news conference later, Christopher declared that there was no place in the new Europe "for an unreformed dictatorship that refuses to heed the will of its people."

His words were echoed by French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, who said NATO "must make clear to the Serb leaders that we are not ready to accept the continuation of behaviour contrary to the universally accepted rules of democracy".

At a meeting in Brussels on Tuesday evening with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, Christopher attempted to swing Moscow, which has traditionally taken a pro-Serbian stance, behind international condemnation of Belgrade.
"The Secretary went into some detail about how he thought that Milosevic by his anti-democratic actions was isolating himself," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

"The Secretary said that we were in touch with Milosevic and his advisers to try to get them to reverse themselves on this issue and certainly he felt that effort would be stronger if Russia joined that effort," Burns said.
Primakov did not say whether Russia would do so, he added.

Washington has frequently said that it retains the right to seek to reimpose the U.N. trade sanctions on rump Yugoslavia -- Serbia and Montenegro -- that were lifted after last year's Dayton peace accord on Bosnia.
But Russia and possibly other Security Council members are seen as highly unlikely to agree. Burns did not say whether Christopher had raised the issue with Primakov.
The United States has never lifted its own "outer wall" of sanctions which deny Belgrade a seat in the United Nations and loans from international financial institutions.
Burns confirmed that the United States had cancelled a meeting between the Serbian president and U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum.
He said Kornblum had planned to meet Milosevic in Belgrade later this week after the NATO meeting but Washington had decided that contacts through the U.S. embassy in Belgrade were sufficient.
"There's no need for John to go," he said, adding that the United States planned to wait and see what further action Milosevic took on the elections.
